overall: The AG found the Board deliberated outside a meeting, through its assistant and by the chair's emails to a quorum, before its April 29, 2015 meeting; violations were intentional, referred to hearing, with a recommended $1,000 penalty.

allegations.summary: Board members allegedly deliberated about the complainant's discipline through the Board's assistant before the April 29, 2015 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: A public body may not use a non-member, such as a staff member, to communicate on matters that the Board would not otherwise be able to discuss outside an open meeting.

allegations.summary: The Board chair allegedly deliberated outside a meeting by emailing her opinion on the complainant's discipline to a quorum of the Board twice before April 29, 2015.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, Ms. Pacheco violated the Open Meeting Law by sending her opinion by email to a quorum of the Board on two occasions leading up to the Board's April 29, 2015 meeting.

remedy: Recommended civil penalty of $1,000 under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c) for the intentional violations.
Order of immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Matter referred to a hearing pursuant to 940 CMR 29.07(3).
remedy_passage: We recommend the imposition of a civil penalty of $1,000 and an order of immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
